analyst_view.overall: Early view: a Merseyside derby between sixth and fourth, with Everton on back-to-back wins and Liverpool holding the most away points in the league. Liverpool are also in the Champions League and face Manchester United the weekend before, and Dominik Szoboszlai's knee is a worry. Everton have been without Jack Grealish for disciplinary reasons.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. Liverpool have been far better away than at home, with three goals at Palace, while Everton have won their last two and Thierno Barry is scoring. Both point to goals, but derbies are often cagey, so I stay with the site.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners, six of them Liverpool's. That fits Liverpool having more of the ball at Everton's ground, and nothing in the news changes it.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.1 cards. I lean slightly higher: Liverpool had four players booked at Palace, including Ronald Araujo and Alexis Mac Allister, and a derby adds edge on both sides. Five or six bookings would fit.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.4 shots, a lot for a derby. I lean slightly lower: Everton's last away win was a 1-0 at Newcastle, which suggests Moyes is happy to keep games tight, and Liverpool may be without Szoboszlai.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. Isak, Wirtz and Mac Allister all scored at Palace, and Barry is in form for Everton, so the figure looks fair.
